thread:
Alex: Quick q — we're designing scoped read-only views for audit logs. Need clarity on who should see tenant audit events by default: tenant-admins only, or should we allow members with scoped tokens for more granular/partner access? Also: customer-facing audit exports/signing — do we sign per-tenant keys or platform-level?

Marina: Prefer least-privilege out of the box. Default: tenant-admins get full event visibility. Members should only be able to read events tied to resources they already have access to. Scoped tokens make sense for partners/integrations. @Samir will have thoughts on exact policy syntax. :eyes:

Samir: +1. Scoped tokens are the right primitive. Example policy idea (very minimal):
```json
{
  "principal": "token:abc",
  "allowed": [
    "audit.read:tenant:tenant_123",
    "audit.read:route:/services/service-xyz/events"
  ],
  "exp": "2026-06-01T12:00:00Z",
  "meta": { "issued_by": "platform-integration" }
}
```
Short-lived tokens + route constraints reduce blast radius. Also recommend issuing tokens with a `subject_type` so we can distinguish human-vs-service access in audits.

Jordana: From CS: customers request "immutable signed exports" for SOC2/ISO. They get nervous if platform signs everything with a shared key. We should capture expectations: hosted customers vs private deployment customers.

Marina: Right — for Private we can plug in customer KMS (tenant-managed keys) and sign exports directly. For hosted we can offer two options: (1) platform-signed exports with demonstrable key management + audit trail, or (2) per-tenant derived keys stored in KMS (customer-managed for enterprise) when available. We must document differences clearly.

security-bot: FYI: audit-schema doc posted here https://redwood.dev/docs/audit-schema — also note vulnerability surface: do NOT log raw signing material. Ensure any export/sign flow never writes private key bytes to mutable logs. :warning:

Samir: Operational approach for hosted: create ephemeral signing keys per export, envelope-encrypt those with our master KMS key. That way exported blobs are signed, but we never persist raw tenant signing keys. Also: we must validate event schema before signing. Minimal required fields: `event_id`, `actor`, `actor_role`, `resource_type`, `resource_id`, `action`, `timestamp`, `request_id`, `tenant_id`. Example event shape we should validate against before marking an export as "signed":
```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_01G...",
  "tenant_id": "tenant_123",
  "actor": { "id": "user_9", "type": "user" },
  "actor_role": "admin",
  "resource": { "type": "deployment", "id": "dep_77" },
  "action": "model.update",
  "timestamp": "2026-05-12T15:22:08Z",
  "request_id": "req_abc123",
  "details": { "fields_changed": ["weights_config"] }
}
```
Validation failures should produce a machine-readable report and prevent signing.

eng-sre-oncall: One practical ask: SRE often needs time-limited cross-tenant audit access during incidents. We can't give persistent cross-tenant perms. Proposal: `sre:incident` role that requires two-person approve and request gets logged as an audit event itself; TTL like 30 minutes automatically revoked. That keeps the trail auditable.

Marina: Agreed. Implement `elevated_access` flow: request -> approver -> issue ephemeral scoped token with `audit.read:tenant:*` and `elevation_context` in token. Token TTL 30m, and we add `elevation_context` to audit schema so exports show why access was granted. We'll include `elevation_context` as an optional field on events: {"requested_by":"alice","approver":"bob","reason":"incident triage","expires_at":"..."}.

Alex: Nice. Action items: Samir drafts formal token policy + sample code for scoped tokens (include route/time constraints). Marina drafts KMS options doc (hosted envelope pattern vs customer-managed keys) and updates the schema page to include `elevation_context`. eng-sre to prototype two-person approval flow and TTL enforcement. I'll open a JIRA to track and assign owners. Thanks all :thumbsup:

(Edited to add) security-bot: small note — add a retention-visibility check: make sure retention policy doesn't allow members to request exports longer than their allowed retention window.
